bib.title: 9 Machine learning on knowledge graphs: A primer approach (Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action)
authors: Negro et al. (inferred: from repo notes; the chapter text carries no byline)
bib.venue: Manning book chapter (year inferred from repo notes)

question: What machine learning tasks exist on knowledge graphs, and how do you turn graph data into features for them?
hypothesis: Feature engineering, especially domain-informed features such as homophily, matters more than generic embeddings for graph ML.
contributions: Taxonomy of node-focused and graph-focused ML tasks
Karate club worked example comparing degree, Node2Vec and homophily-degree features

results.claim: Degree-only node features give weighted F1 of about 0.43 on karate-club faction prediction.
results.setup: Karate club, 34 nodes, 60/40 split (random_state=0), weighted precision/recall/F1, standardised features + LogisticRegressionCV (liblinear, ovr, max_iter=1000); degree-only embedding

results.claim: Node2Vec (64-d) features give weighted F1 of about 0.64 on the same task.
results.setup: Karate club, 34 nodes, 60/40 split (random_state=0), weighted precision/recall/F1, standardised features + LogisticRegressionCV (liblinear, ovr, max_iter=1000); Node2Vec dimensions=64, walk_length=30, num_walks=200, window=10

results.claim: Hand-built homophily features (total degree, Mr. Hi degree, Officer degree) give weighted F1 of about 0.93.
results.setup: Karate club, 34 nodes, 60/40 split (random_state=0), weighted precision/recall/F1, standardised features + LogisticRegressionCV (liblinear, ovr, max_iter=1000); 3-element degree vector
results.note: Text then says results are 'very stable and always close to 100%', which is looser than the printed 0.927; no repeated-run numbers given.

results.claim: Repeated runs of the degree and Node2Vec setups fluctuate widely, between 30% and 70% F1.
results.setup: Karate club, 34 nodes, 60/40 split (random_state=0), weighted precision/recall/F1, standardised features + LogisticRegressionCV (liblinear, ovr, max_iter=1000); degree and Node2Vec setups, multiple executions
results.quote: with f-scores fluctuating widely between 30% and 70%
results.note: Number of runs not stated; not stated what varies between runs (split is fixed in listing 9.6).

results.claim: Louvain (seed=123) on the karate club graph finds four communities, all but one pure in club membership (one spurious node, number 8).
results.setup: networkx louvain_communities(G, seed=123) on karate club graph
results.quote: This code identifies four communities, as shown in figure 9.13.

results.claim: Node classification breaks the i.i.d. assumption because nodes are interconnected, so models must use both node features and network relationships.
results.quote: node classification shatters this i.i.d. assumption

limits: Single 34-node graph, 14 test nodes, no repeated-split statistics; F1 differences are weakly supported.
Homophily features use neighbours' club labels (Mr. Hi / Officer), which are the target labels, so they leak labels; chapter does not discuss this.
Node2Vec p and q are not given; only 'requires careful tuning' and an exercise with lower walk_length/num_walks is offered, no tuned result.
Chapter text says Louvain was discussed in chapter 4; GNNs deferred to chapters 10-12.
Prose says Node2Vec 'considers 10 nodes before and after' and walks 'each visiting 30 nodes'; per-node walk count not stated in text.
practices: Use the same featurization at training and prediction time (Note after Fig 9.8).
Express domain knowledge such as homophily as features before reaching for embeddings (9.3.1).
Tune autonomous embeddings such as Node2Vec; do not assume defaults are good (9.3.1).

terms.definition: The entire dataset is represented as one graph, with nodes and relationships as the data points.
The data consists of a set of graphs, and each data point is an entire graph.
Predicting the existence of a connection between two nodes; relationship prediction also predicts the type.
A fast method for detecting communities that propagates labels through the network; nodes with the same label end in the same community; non-deterministic.
